    Section 9: successors and endpoint types #

    def:primitive-characters, set:fixed-character, def:successor-types: for a positive primitive character χ ∈ L, q̂_x = q_x if q_x ≠ 0 and ℓ(q_x) = χ, and 0 otherwise. A nonidentity ray is shiftable if a ray with the same endpoints has weight ℓ(r) + χ (its successor r⁺). The successor is obtained by one local generator of character χ (succ_by_gen), which gives the three endpoint types L, R, B. Also lem:primitive-action-generation.

    References #

    • Multiplicative bases and deformations of representation-finite algebras, https://github.com/haruhisa-enomoto/multiplicative-bases-deformations. Numbered statements cited here refer to it.

      theorem LargeIndecomposable.RaySys.Sys.prim_action_gen {V R L : Type} [AddCommGroup L] [DecidableEq L] [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] [Fintype R] [DecidableEq R] (S : Sys V R L) {f : R} (hf : S.IsGen f) (hprim : Prim (S.χ (S.P.src f))) (hqf : S.q (S.P.src f) * S.rr f ≠ 0) :
      S.CycL f ∧ (S.CycR f → S.χ (S.P.tgt f) = S.χ (S.P.src f) ∧ S.q (S.P.src f) * S.rr f = S.rr f * S.q (S.P.tgt f))

      Lemma 9.4 (lem:primitive-action-generation): for f generating with ℓ(q_x) primitive and q_x f ≠ 0, the Hom is cyclic at x; if it is also cyclic at y, then ℓ(q_y) = ℓ(q_x) and q_x f = f q_y.
